**Subject:** Pre-Authorization Requirement Update — Scheduling Impact for Certain Procedures

---

**To:** Dermatology Clinical Staff
**From:** [Your Name/Department]
**Date:** [Date]

---

Team,

Starting [effective date], a new pre-authorization requirement from [Payer Name] will add approximately **48 hours** to approval timelines for certain procedures. Here is what this means for your scheduling and your patients.

---

**Patient Flow Impact**

Affected procedures will no longer be schedulable within a 48-hour window unless authorization is already confirmed. Patients arriving for these appointments without prior approval will need to be rescheduled or converted to a consultation visit, which adds an average of **10–15 minutes** to front-desk handling per affected appointment. Procedure rooms should remain available as planned — the impact is upstream, at the scheduling and intake stage, not in the exam room.

Affected procedure codes are listed in the attached reference sheet. Please do not include specific case details in any reply to this email.

---

**New Scheduling Process**

When booking an affected procedure:

1. Verify the procedure code against the attached list before confirming the appointment.
2. Submit the pre-authorization request at the time of scheduling, not at check-in.
3. Confirm authorization is on file before the patient's appointment date.
4. Flag any unresolved authorizations to the billing team by end of day, two business days before the appointment.
5. Notify the patient that their appointment is pending insurance confirmation.

---

**If the Authorization Portal Is Unavailable**

If the payer portal is down at the time of scheduling, do not hold the appointment slot open without a confirmed authorization. Instead:

- Submit the request by fax to [Payer Fax Number] using the paper form located in [specific location, e.g., front desk drawer / shared drive folder].
- Note "portal unavailable — fax submitted" in the scheduling record with the date and time.
- Follow up via portal the next business day to confirm receipt.

This keeps the 48-hour clock running even when the system isn't cooperating.

---

**Questions**

For questions about which procedures are affected, contact [Billing Contact Name/Role] at [internal extension or secure contact method]. For scheduling workflow questions, reach [Office Manager Name/Role].

Please avoid including appointment-specific or case-specific details in email replies — use your internal system for anything patient-related.

Thank you for your flexibility as we work through this change.

[Your Name]
[Title]
[Clinic Name]

**Subject:** Pre-Authorization Requirement Update — Scheduling Impact for Certain Procedures

---

**To:** Dermatology Clinical Staff
**From:** [Your Name/Department]
**Date:** [Date]

---

Team,

Starting [effective date], certain procedures will require insurance pre-authorization before an appointment can be confirmed. Here is what that looks like for patients and for scheduling.

---

**What Changes for Patients**

Patients booking affected procedures will need to wait for insurance confirmation before their appointment is finalized — a window of approximately **48 hours**. Any patient who arrives without a confirmed authorization will need to be rescheduled or converted to a consultation visit, which adds an average of **10–15 minutes** of front-desk handling per affected appointment. Procedure rooms are not impacted; this change is contained entirely to the scheduling and intake stage.

[Payer Name] is requiring this as of [effective date]. The affected procedure codes are listed in the attached reference sheet. Please do not include case-specific details in any reply to this email.

---

**Updated Scheduling Steps**

For any appointment involving an affected procedure code:

1. Verify the code against the attached list before confirming the appointment.
2. Submit the pre-authorization request at the time of scheduling — not at check-in.
3. Confirm authorization is on file at least two business days before the appointment.
4. Flag any unresolved authorizations to the billing team by end of day on that two-day mark.
5. Notify the patient that their appointment is pending insurance confirmation.

---

**If the Authorization Portal Is Unavailable**

If the payer portal is down when a request needs to be submitted, do not hold the appointment slot open without confirmed authorization. Instead:

- Fax the request to [Payer Fax Number] using the paper form at [specific location, e.g., front desk drawer / shared drive folder].
- Enter "portal unavailable — fax submitted" in the scheduling system, with date and time.
- Check the portal the next business day to confirm the fax was received.

This keeps the 48-hour clock running regardless of system availability.

---

**Questions**

For questions about affected procedure codes, contact [Billing Contact Name/Role] at [internal extension or secure contact method]. For scheduling workflow questions, reach [Office Manager Name/Role].

Use your internal system for anything appointment- or case-specific — email is not a secure channel for those details.

Thank you,

[Your Name]
[Title]
[Clinic Name]

**Subject:** Pre-Authorization Requirement Update — Scheduling Impact for Certain Procedures

---

**To:** Dermatology Clinical Staff
**From:** [Your Name/Department]
**Date:** [Date]

---

Team,

Starting [effective date], certain procedures will require insurance pre-authorization before an appointment can be confirmed. Here is what that looks like for patients and for scheduling.

---

**What Changes for Patients**

Patients booking affected procedures will need to wait for insurance confirmation before their appointment is finalized — a window of approximately **48 hours**. Any patient who arrives without a confirmed authorization will need to be rescheduled or converted to a consultation visit, which adds an average of **10–15 minutes** of front-desk handling per affected appointment. Procedure rooms are not impacted; this change is contained entirely to the scheduling and intake stage.

[Payer Name] is requiring this as of [effective date]. The affected procedure codes are listed in the attached reference sheet. Please do not include case-specific details in any reply to this email.

---

**Updated Scheduling Steps**

For any appointment involving an affected procedure code:

1. Verify the code against the attached list before confirming the appointment.
2. Submit the pre-authorization request at the time of scheduling — not at check-in.
3. Confirm authorization is on file at least two business days before the appointment.
4. Flag any unresolved authorizations to the billing team by end of day on that two-day mark.
5. Notify the patient that their appointment is pending insurance confirmation.

---

**If the Authorization Portal Is Unavailable**

If the payer portal is down when a request needs to be submitted, the fax process below completes the submission fully — the 48-hour clock starts from the fax timestamp, and the appointment can advance to the confirmation stage as normal:

1. Fax the request to [Payer Fax Number] using the paper pre-auth form stored at [specific location, e.g., front desk drawer / shared drive folder].
2. Enter "portal unavailable — fax submitted" in the scheduling system with the date and time.
3. Check the portal the next business day to confirm receipt and pull the authorization number into the record.

This is a complete alternate submission path, not a holding pattern. Staff do not need to wait for the portal to come back online before moving the appointment forward.

---

**Questions**

For questions about affected procedure codes, contact [Billing Contact Name/Role] at [internal extension or secure contact method]. For scheduling workflow questions, reach [Office Manager Name/Role].

Use your internal system for anything appointment- or case-specific — email is not a secure channel for those details.

Thank you,

[Your Name]
[Title]
[Clinic Name]
